questions: Does the ±0.05 m spread keep at least one sensor reading above 0.05 total at the largest lateral error seen on each track, so line_loss_events goes to 0?
Does the 16 mm footprint lower signal resolution near centre (more dead zone around zero), and does this raise steering_oscillation or rms_error on the s-bend and slalom?
Which track ends the run first now, and at what progress? Is it still off_track, or does it stall?
With the wider spread, is the signal range still within about ±2 at the sensor weights you chose?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line_loss_events is still above 0 with this layout, report the max_error at the first loss. If steering_oscillation rises sharply with no change in line_loss_events, the 16 mm footprint may be the cause, and I will revert to 12 mm with the same spread.

intent: Remove the line-loss failure that ends every current run. Widen the sensor spread from ±0.03 m to ±0.05 m and grow the footprint from 12 mm to 16 mm, so the line stays detected out to about 0.07 m offset and the robot is not pushed to the 0.06 m off-track limit before it can correct. Keep the other geometry fixed so the change in race results can be attributed to the sensing layout.
learning: Baseline race data showed that the 0.06 m off-track limit is fixed by the contract (body width cannot widen it), so the failure comes from losing the line at about 0.045 to 0.05 m offset, not from the body. Iteration 1 tests whether widening sensor spread and footprint removes that loss. Key measurements next: line_loss_events, max_error at first loss, and progress per track.
rationale: The race evidence (entityR2A, 60 trials) shows every run ending off_track, with max_error about 0.06 m, one line_loss_event per run, and progress of only 0.035 to 0.11. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). With body_width 0.12 that is 0.06 m, and widening the body to its 0.18 maximum still gives 0.06 m, so body width cannot buy margin. The robot has to stay within 0.06 m of the centre line. The line-loss event means the tape left every sensor's reach at about 0.05 m offset. The baseline sensors span only ±0.03 m with 12 mm footprints, so the tape (half-width 0.0125 m) drops out of all sensors once the robot is roughly 0.045 to 0.05 m off centre. The controller then falls back to a fixed search at 0.35 throttle and the robot drifts off. I therefore change the sensing geometry, not the body: widen the sensor spread to ±0.05 m (x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 at y = 0.04) so the line stays visible out to about 0.07 m offset, and enlarge the footprint to 16 mm so each sensor's coverage of the tape grows and the readings do not fall below the 0.05 total-reading threshold at the edges. I keep the 0.04 m forward offset, 0.12 m wheel track, 0.03 m wheel radius and 0.7 kg mass, so the only variables that change are sensor spread and footprint. Expected result: line_loss_events drop toward 0, the off_track endings become rarer, progress rises well above 0.11 on the oval, and rms_error falls below the current 0.03 m. Risk: a wider spread on the tight s-bend and slalom may reduce signal resolution near centre, so I ask for rms_error by track to check this. The wheel track and controller gains stay for the Integrator to tune.
